contentBlocks.body: Map is useful when keys are discovered while your program runs. Read the old count with get, provide a default when it is missing, then set the next count.
**Worked example.** A missing key starts at zero. Each occurrence reads the old count, increments it, and writes the new count. Map distinguishes a missing key from a stored value through has.
The number of keys measures distinct words, not the total number of occurrences.

**Try a small change.** Predict counts.size and the sum of all counts. Explain the difference.

Then complete the independent check below without copying the example. Explain the boundary case in words before running it.

payload.text: Use counts.____(key) to read the previous value and counts.set(key, next) to store the update.
